title: "NFL Draft Predictor | Model 1 — Logistic Regression"
output: html_document
---

# Model 1 — Logistic Regression

Baseline: size + position, matching File 02. Improvement: add the combine drills and missing-test indicators. I compare **5-fold cross-validated Kappa and Accuracy** using `caret::train()` as taught in class, select the better specification using training data only, and generate a single probability for each held-out prospect.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
dir.create("objects", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
train_data <- readRDS("objects/train_data.rds")
test_data <- readRDS("objects/test_data.rds")
train_x_raw <- readRDS("objects/train_x_raw.rds")
test_x_raw <- readRDS("objects/test_x_raw.rds")
train_y <- readRDS("objects/train_y.rds")
```


```{r analysis}
library(caret)
set.seed(12345)
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5, classProbs = TRUE)

# Initial model: draft outcome explained by position and physical size.
baseline_train <- data.frame(Drafted = train_y,
                             train_x_raw[, c("pos_group", "InchHeight", "wt")])
base_logit <- train(Drafted ~ ., data = baseline_train, method = "glm",
                    family = binomial(), metric = "Kappa", trControl = ctrl)

# Improved model: add test scores and flags showing which drills were missing.
expanded_train <- data.frame(Drafted = train_y, train_x_raw)
set.seed(12345)
expanded_logit <- train(Drafted ~ ., data = expanded_train, method = "glm",
                        family = binomial(), metric = "Kappa", trControl = ctrl)

logit_cv <- data.frame(Version = c("Size and position", "Combine drills added"),
                       Accuracy = c(base_logit$results$Accuracy[1], expanded_logit$results$Accuracy[1]),
                       Kappa = c(base_logit$results$Kappa[1], expanded_logit$results$Kappa[1]))
print(logit_cv)
# Select the version with higher CV Kappa; Accuracy breaks ties.
choice <- order(-logit_cv$Kappa, -logit_cv$Accuracy)[1]
logit_model <- if (choice == 1) base_logit else expanded_logit
logit_test_x <- if (choice == 1) test_x_raw[, c("pos_group", "InchHeight", "wt")] else test_x_raw
logit_prob <- as.numeric(predict(logit_model, newdata = logit_test_x, type = "prob")[, "Drafted"])
logit_pred <- factor(ifelse(logit_prob >= 0.5, "Drafted", "Undrafted"),
                     levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted"))
```


## **3.1 Baseline Logistic Regression**

```{r}
logmodel <- glm(Drafted ~ ., data = train_data, family = "binomial")
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(broom)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)
library(pscl)
library(tibble)
library(htmltools)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Extract regression results and confidence intervals
# --------------------------------------------------

reg_results <- tidy(logmodel, conf.int = TRUE)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Format regression coefficients
# --------------------------------------------------

reg_table <- reg_results %>%
  mutate(
    stars = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      p.value < 0.10  ~ ".",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),

    relationship = case_when(
      term == "(Intercept)" ~ "",
      estimate > 0 ~ "+",
      estimate < 0 ~ "\u2212",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),

    # NFL colors for coefficients
    coefficient_color = ifelse(
      estimate >= 0, "#013369", "#D50A0A"
    ),

    # Stack coefficient, standard error, and CI
    results = paste0(
      "<span style='color:", coefficient_color,
      "; font-weight:bold;'>",
      sprintf("%.4f%s", estimate, stars),
      "</span>",
      "<br>(",
      sprintf("%.4f", std.error),
      ")<br>[",
      sprintf("%.4f", conf.low),
      ", ",
      sprintf("%.4f", conf.high),
      "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Variables = term,
    `Exp. Relationship` = relationship,
    `Logistic Regression` = results
  )

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate model statistics
# --------------------------------------------------

n_obs <- nobs(logmodel)

pseudo_r2 <- unname(
  pscl::pR2(logmodel)["McFadden"]
)

aic_score <- AIC(logmodel)

fisher_iterations <- logmodel$iter

# Append model statistics at the bottom of the table
reg_table <- bind_rows(
  reg_table,

  tibble(
    Variables = c(
      "n (Sample)",
      "McFadden Pseudo-R²",
      "AIC",
      "Fisher Scoring Iterations"
    ),

    `Exp. Relationship` = c("", "", "", ""),

    `Logistic Regression` = c(
      format(n_obs, big.mark = ","),
      sprintf("%.5f", pseudo_r2),
      sprintf("%.2f", aic_score),
      as.character(fisher_iterations)
    )
  )
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Identify row positions for formatting
# --------------------------------------------------

positive_rows <- which(
  reg_table[["Exp. Relationship"]] == "+"
)

negative_rows <- which(
  reg_table[["Exp. Relationship"]] == "\u2212"
)

# Identify all four model statistics rows
model_rows <- which(
  reg_table$Variables %in% c(
    "n (Sample)",
    "McFadden Pseudo-R²",
    "AIC",
    "Fisher Scoring Iterations"
  )
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Create ONE unified regression table
# --------------------------------------------------

reg_gt <- gt(reg_table) %>%

  # Render stacked HTML results
  fmt_markdown(
    columns = `Logistic Regression`
  ) %>%

  # Table title
  tab_header(
    title = md("**LOGISTIC REGRESSION RESULTS**")
  ) %>%

  # Column headers
  cols_label(
    Variables = "Variables",
    `Exp. Relationship` = "Exp. Relationship",
    `Logistic Regression` = "Logistic Regression"
  ) %>%

  # Center columns
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = everything()
  ) %>%

  # Column widths
  cols_width(
    Variables ~ px(250),
    `Exp. Relationship` ~ px(180),
    `Logistic Regression` ~ px(350)
  ) %>%

  # Table dimensions and borders
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(15),

    heading.title.font.size = px(23),
    heading.title.font.weight = "bold",

    column_labels.background.color = "#013369",
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold",

    table.border.top.color = "#D50A0A",
    table.border.top.width = px(4),

    table.border.bottom.color = "#013369",
    table.border.bottom.width = px(3),

    table_body.hlines.color = "#CCD6E0",
    table_body.hlines.width = px(1)
  ) %>%

  # NFL navy title
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(
      color = "#013369",
      weight = "bold"
    ),
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  ) %>%

  # White column header text
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(
      color = "white",
      weight = "bold"
    ),
    locations = cells_column_labels(
      columns = everything()
    )
  ) %>%

  # Bold all variable names
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(
      weight = "bold"
    ),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = Variables
    )
  ) %>%

  # Positive relationship indicators: NFL navy
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(
      color = "#013369",
      weight = "bold"
    ),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = `Exp. Relationship`,
      rows = positive_rows
    )
  ) %>%

  # Negative relationship indicators: NFL red
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(
      color = "#D50A0A",
      weight = "bold"
    ),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = `Exp. Relationship`,
      rows = negative_rows
    )
  ) %>%

  # Alternating light-blue rows
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(
      color = "#E8EFF6"
    ),
    locations = cells_body(
      rows = seq(2, nrow(reg_table), by = 2)
    )
  ) %>%

  # Highlight all four model statistics rows
  # This styling comes AFTER alternating row styling
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#013369"),
      cell_text(
        color = "white",
        weight = "bold"
      )
    ),
    locations = cells_body(
      rows = model_rows
    )
  ) %>%

  # Footnote
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md(
      "Note: Logistic regression coefficients are unstandardized.
      Standard errors are in parentheses, followed by 95% confidence
      intervals. *** p < 0.001, ** p < 0.01, * p < 0.05,
      . p < 0.10."
    )
  )

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Add collapsible functionality to the SAME table
# --------------------------------------------------

htmltools::tagList(

  # Toggle button above the table
  htmltools::tags$button(
    id = "toggle-regression-variables",

    type = "button",

    "Show Regression Variables and Relationships",

    style = paste(
      "background: none;",
      "border: none;",
      "color: #013369;",
      "font-weight: bold;",
      "font-size: 16px;",
      "cursor: pointer;",
      "padding: 12px 0;",
      "margin-bottom: 8px;"
    ),

    `aria-expanded` = "false"
  ),

  # Render the complete original table
  htmltools::div(
    id = "logistic-regression-table",

    htmltools::HTML(
      gt::as_raw_html(reg_gt)
    )
  ),

  # JavaScript to hide/show only regression variables
  htmltools::tags$script(
    htmltools::HTML("
      (function() {

        const button = document.getElementById(
          'toggle-regression-variables'
        );

        const container = document.getElementById(
          'logistic-regression-table'
        );

        if (!button || !container) return;

        const table = container.querySelector('table');

        if (!table) return;

        // These four rows must ALWAYS remain visible
        const statsNames = [
          'n (Sample)',
          'McFadden Pseudo-R²',
          'AIC',
          'Fisher Scoring Iterations'
        ];

        // Get all body rows from the ONE table
        const rows = Array.from(
          table.querySelectorAll('tbody tr')
        );

        // Identify only regression-variable rows
        const variableRows = rows.filter(row => {

          const firstCell = row.querySelector('th, td');

          if (!firstCell) return false;

          const label = firstCell.textContent
            .replace(/\\s+/g, ' ')
            .trim();

          return !statsNames.includes(label);

        });

        // Initially hide regression variables
        variableRows.forEach(row => {
          row.style.display = 'none';
        });

        let expanded = false;

        // Toggle visibility when clicked
        button.addEventListener('click', function() {

          expanded = !expanded;

          variableRows.forEach(row => {
            row.style.display = expanded ? '' : 'none';
          });

          button.textContent = expanded
            ? 'Hide Regression Variables and Relationships'
            : 'Show Regression Variables and Relationships';

          button.setAttribute(
            'aria-expanded',
            String(expanded)
          );

        });

      })();
    ")
  )
)
```


## **3.2 Logistic Regression with Linear Effects**

```{r correlation_matrix, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, fig.align='center', out.width='100%', echo=FALSE}
library(corrplot)

# Select numeric variables and exclude missing indicators
train_numeric <- train_data[, 
  sapply(train_data, is.numeric) & 
  !grepl("_missing$", names(train_data))
]

# Calculate correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(train_numeric,
                  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
                  method = "pearson")

# Display correlation matrix
round(cor_matrix, 3)

# Visualize correlation matrix
corrplot(cor_matrix,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.srt = 45,
         number.cex = 0.7)
```


```{r}
# Full logistic regression model with interaction effects

logmodel_linear <- glm(
  Drafted ~ . +

    # ==========================================
    # 1. POSITION-SPECIFIC INTERACTIONS
    # ==========================================

    pos_group * InchHeight +
    # Assumption: The effect of height on draft probability
    # differs depending on the player's position.

    pos_group * wt +
    # Assumption: The effect of weight on draft probability
    # differs depending on the player's position.

    pos_group * forty +
    # Assumption: The effect of 40-yard dash performance
    # differs depending on the player's position.

    pos_group * vertical +
    # Assumption: The effect of vertical jump performance
    # differs depending on the player's position.

    pos_group * bench +
    # Assumption: The effect of upper-body strength
    # differs depending on the player's position.

    pos_group * broad_jump +
    # Assumption: The effect of horizontal explosiveness
    # differs depending on the player's position.

    pos_group * cone +
    # Assumption: The effect of agility performance
    # differs depending on the player's position.

    pos_group * shuttle +

    # Assumption: The effect of short-distance agility
    # differs depending on the player's position.


    # ==========================================
    # 2. PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTIC INTERACTIONS
    # ==========================================

    InchHeight * wt +
    # Assumption: The combination of height and weight
    # provides additional information about draft probability.

    wt * forty +
    # Assumption: The relationship between speed and draft
    # probability depends on the player's weight.

    wt * vertical +
    # Assumption: The relationship between explosiveness
    # and draft probability depends on the player's weight.

    wt * bench +
    # Assumption: The predictive importance of strength
    # depends on the player's weight.


    # ==========================================
    # 3. ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE INTERACTIONS
    # ==========================================

    forty * vertical +
    # Assumption: The combination of speed and vertical
    # explosiveness provides additional predictive information.

    forty * cone +
    # Assumption: The relationship between straight-line
    # speed and agility influences draft probability.

    forty * shuttle, 
    # Assumption: The combination of speed and short-distance
    # agility provides additional predictive information.

  data = train_data,
  family = "binomial"
)
```

## **3.3 Logistic Regression with Nonlinear Effects** 

```{r}
# Full logistic regression model with interaction effects

logmodel_nonlinear <- glm(
  Drafted ~ . +
    
    # ==========================================
    # 4. NON-LINEAR EFFECTS (SQUARED TERMS)
    # ==========================================

    I(InchHeight^2) +
    # Assumption: Height has a potentially curved relationship with draft probability.

    I(wt^2) +
    # Assumption: There may be an optimal weight range for draft selection.

    I(forty^2) +
    # Assumption: The relationship between speed and draft probability is non-linear.

    I(vertical^2) +
    # Assumption: The effect of vertical explosiveness may have diminishing returns.

    I(bench^2) +
    # Assumption: The effect of strength may have diminishing returns.

    I(broad_jump^2) +
    # Assumption: The relationship between horizontal explosiveness and draft probability is non-linear.

    I(cone^2) +
    # Assumption: The effect of agility may be non-linear.

    I(shuttle^2),
    # Assumption: The effect of short-distance agility may be non-linear.


  data = train_data,
  family = "binomial"
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}

    ),

    ),

    # Stack coefficient, standard error, and CI

      "<span style='color:", coefficient_color,
      "; font-weight:bold;'>",
      sprintf("%.4f%s", estimate, stars),
      "</span>",

      ")<br>[",

      ", ",
      sprintf("%.4f", conf.high),
      "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Variables = term,
    `Exp. Relationship` = relationship,
    `Logistic Regression` = results
  )

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate model statistics
# --------------------------------------------------

pseudo_r2 <- unname(
  pscl::pR2(logmodel_nonlinear)["McFadden"]
)

aic_score <- AIC(logmodel_nonlinear)

# Append model statistics at the bottom

  reg_table,

  tibble(
    Variables = c(
      "n (Sample)",
      "McFadden Pseudo-R²",

    ),

    )
  )
)

        const statsNames = [

          'McFadden Pseudo-R²',
          'AIC',
          'Fisher Scoring Iterations'
        ];

          table.querySelectorAll('tbody tr')
        );

        // Identify regression-variable rows
        const variableRows = rows.filter(row => {

          const firstCell = row.querySelector('th, td');

          if (!firstCell) return false;

          const label = firstCell.textContent
            .replace(/\\s+/g, ' ')
            .trim();

          return !statsNames.includes(label);

        });

        // Initially hide regression variables
        variableRows.forEach(row => {
          row.style.display = 'none';

        button.addEventListener('click', function() {

          expanded = !expanded;

          variableRows.forEach(row => {

            ? 'Hide Regression Variables and Relationships'

  )
```

## **3.4 Final Model Selection: Backward AIC**

```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)

# Variables to center
continuous_vars <- c(
  "season",
  "InchHeight",
  "wt",
  "forty",
  "vertical",
  "bench",
  "broad_jump",
  "cone",
  "shuttle"
)

# Calculate means from training data only
center_means <- sapply(
  train_data[continuous_vars],
  mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Center training and test data
for (v in continuous_vars) {

  train_data[[paste0(v, "_c")]] <-
    train_data[[v]] - center_means[[v]]

  test_data[[paste0(v, "_c")]] <-
    test_data[[v]] - center_means[[v]]
}

# Check that variables have been created
names(train_data)
names(test_data)
```


```{r}
Model_full <- glm(

  Drafted ~

    # ----------------------------------------
    # 1. MAIN EFFECTS
    # ----------------------------------------

    season_c +
    pos_group +

    InchHeight_c +
    wt_c +
    forty_c +
    vertical_c +
    bench_c +
    broad_jump_c +
    cone_c +
    shuttle_c +

    # Missingness indicators
    InchHeight_missing +
    wt_missing +
    forty_missing +
    vertical_missing +
    bench_missing +
    broad_jump_missing +
    cone_missing +
    shuttle_missing +


    # ----------------------------------------
    # 2. POSITION-SPECIFIC INTERACTIONS
    # ----------------------------------------

    pos_group:InchHeight_c +
    # Height has different importance across positions.

    pos_group:wt_c +
    # Optimal weight requirements differ across positions.

    pos_group:forty_c +
    # The importance of speed differs across positions.

    pos_group:vertical_c +
    # Vertical explosiveness matters differently across positions.

    pos_group:bench_c +
    # Strength requirements differ across positions.

    pos_group:broad_jump_c +
    # Horizontal explosiveness matters differently across positions.

    pos_group:cone_c +
    # Agility requirements differ across positions.

    pos_group:shuttle_c +
    # Short-distance agility matters differently across positions.


    # ----------------------------------------
    # 3. PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTIC INTERACTIONS
    # ----------------------------------------

    InchHeight_c:wt_c +
    # The combination of height and weight matters.

    wt_c:forty_c +
    # The relationship between weight and speed matters.

    wt_c:vertical_c +
    # Explosiveness depends partly on body weight.

    wt_c:bench_c +
    # The value of strength may depend on body weight.


    # ----------------------------------------
    # 4. ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE INTERACTIONS
    # ----------------------------------------

    forty_c:cone_c +
    # Straight-line speed and agility jointly influence selection.

    forty_c:shuttle_c +
    # Speed and short-distance agility jointly influence selection.


    # ----------------------------------------
    # 5. SEASON-SPECIFIC INTERACTIONS
    # ----------------------------------------

    season_c:forty_c +
    # The importance of speed may change over time.

    season_c:vertical_c +
    # The importance of vertical explosiveness may change over time.

    season_c:wt_c +
    # The importance of weight may change over time.

    season_c:InchHeight_c +
    # The importance of height may change over time.


    # ----------------------------------------
    # 6. NON-LINEAR EFFECTS (QUADRATIC)
    # ----------------------------------------

    I(InchHeight_c^2) +
    # Potential optimal height range.

    I(wt_c^2) +
    # Potential optimal weight range.

    I(forty_c^2) +
    # Non-linear relationship between speed and draft probability.

    I(vertical_c^2) +
    # Potential diminishing returns from vertical explosiveness.

    I(bench_c^2) +
    # Potential diminishing returns from strength.

    I(broad_jump_c^2) +
    # Non-linear relationship with horizontal explosiveness.

    I(cone_c^2) +
    # Non-linear relationship with agility.

    I(shuttle_c^2),
    # Non-linear relationship with short-distance agility.


  data = train_data,

  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)
```

```{r}
Model <- step(Model_full, direction="backward", trace=0)
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}

# 1. Extract regression results and confidence intervals
# --------------------------------------------------

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Format regression coefficients
# --------------------------------------------------

reg_table <- reg_results %>%
  mutate(
    stars = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      p.value < 0.10  ~ ".",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),

    relationship = case_when(
      term == "(Intercept)" ~ "",
      estimate > 0 ~ "+",
      estimate < 0 ~ "\u2212",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),

    # NFL colors for coefficients
    coefficient_color = ifelse(
      estimate >= 0, "#013369", "#D50A0A"
    ),

    # Stack coefficient, standard error, and CI
    results = paste0(
      "<span style='color:", coefficient_color,
      "; font-weight:bold;'>",
      sprintf("%.4f%s", estimate, stars),
      "</span>",
      "<br>(",
      sprintf("%.4f", std.error),
      ")<br>[",
      sprintf("%.4f", conf.low),
      ", ",
      sprintf("%.4f", conf.high),
      "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Variables = term,
    `Exp. Relationship` = relationship,
    `Logistic Regression` = results
  )
```

## **3.5 Predicting Test Data**

### *3.5.1 Cross-Validation for Optimal Classification Threshold*

```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(dplyr)

# Ensure correct outcome coding
train_data$Drafted <- factor(
  ifelse(
    as.character(train_data$Drafted) %in% c("1", "Drafted"),
    "Drafted",
    "Undrafted"
  ),
  levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted")
)

# Five-fold cross-validation
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 5,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  savePredictions = "final",
  summaryFunction = defaultSummary
)

set.seed(12345)

# Estimate logistic regression
cv_model <- train(
  formula(Model),
  data = train_data,
  method = "glm",
  family = binomial(),
  metric = "Kappa",
  trControl = ctrl
)

# Average performance across the five folds
cv_model$results[, c("Accuracy", "Kappa")]

# Extract out-of-fold predictions
cv_predictions <- cv_model$pred

# Candidate thresholds
thresholds <- seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.01)

# Evaluate each threshold
threshold_results <- lapply(thresholds, function(t) {

  predictions <- factor(
    ifelse(
      cv_predictions$Drafted >= t,
      "Drafted",
      "Undrafted"
    ),
    levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted")
  )

  actual <- factor(
    cv_predictions$obs,
    levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted")
  )

  cm <- confusionMatrix(
    predictions,
    actual,
    positive = "Drafted"
  )

  data.frame(
    Threshold = t,
    Accuracy = unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    Kappa = unname(cm$overall["Kappa"]),
    Sensitivity = unname(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
    Specificity = unname(cm$byClass["Specificity"])
  )
})

threshold_results <- bind_rows(threshold_results)

# Find optimal thresholds
best_accuracy <- threshold_results[
  which.max(threshold_results$Accuracy), ]

best_kappa <- threshold_results[
  which.max(threshold_results$Kappa), ]

# Remove unseen position category
test_data_filtered <- test_data %>%
  filter(as.character(pos_group) != "Other")

# Align factor levels
test_data_filtered$pos_group <- factor(
  as.character(test_data_filtered$pos_group),
  levels = levels(train_data$pos_group)
)

stopifnot(!anyNA(test_data_filtered$pos_group))

# Generate predicted probabilities
test_prob <- predict(
  cv_model,
  newdata = test_data_filtered,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Drafted"]

# Actual outcomes
actual_test <- factor(
  ifelse(test_data_filtered$Drafted == 1, "Drafted", "Undrafted"),
  levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted")
)

# Standard threshold
pred_standard <- factor(
  ifelse(test_prob >= 0.50, "Drafted", "Undrafted"),
  levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted")
)

# Accuracy-optimized threshold
pred_accuracy <- factor(
  ifelse(test_prob >= best_accuracy$Threshold, "Drafted", "Undrafted"),
  levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted")
)

# Kappa-optimized threshold
pred_kappa <- factor(
  ifelse(test_prob >= best_kappa$Threshold, "Drafted", "Undrafted"),
  levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted")
)

# Confusion matrices
cm_standard <- confusionMatrix(
  pred_standard, actual_test, positive = "Drafted"
)

cm_accuracy <- confusionMatrix(
  pred_accuracy, actual_test, positive = "Drafted"
)

cm_kappa <- confusionMatrix(
  pred_kappa, actual_test, positive = "Drafted"
)

# Comparison table
final_comparison <- data.frame(
  Method = c(
    "Standard (0.50)",
    "CV Accuracy optimal",
    "CV Kappa optimal"
  ),

  Threshold = c(
    0.50,
    best_accuracy$Threshold,
    best_kappa$Threshold
  ),

  Accuracy = c(
    cm_standard$overall["Accuracy"],
    cm_accuracy$overall["Accuracy"],
    cm_kappa$overall["Accuracy"]
  ),

  Kappa = c(
    cm_standard$overall["Kappa"],
    cm_accuracy$overall["Kappa"],
    cm_kappa$overall["Kappa"]
  ),

  Sensitivity = c(
    cm_standard$byClass["Sensitivity"],
    cm_accuracy$byClass["Sensitivity"],
    cm_kappa$byClass["Sensitivity"]
  ),

  Specificity = c(
    cm_standard$byClass["Specificity"],
    cm_accuracy$byClass["Specificity"],
    cm_kappa$byClass["Specificity"]
  )
)

# Round results
final_comparison[-1] <- lapply(
  final_comparison[-1],
  function(x) round(as.numeric(x), 4)
)

print(final_comparison)
```

### *3.5.2 Final Predictive Model*

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Generate binary predictions using the selected threshold
final_predictions <- ifelse(
  test_prob >= best_kappa$Threshold,
  1,
  0
)

# Actual outcomes
final_actual <- ifelse(
  actual_test == "Drafted",
  1,
  0
)

# Final confusion matrix
final_cm <- confusionMatrix(
  as.factor(final_predictions),
  as.factor(final_actual),
  positive = "1"
)

final_cm
```
